title: The Scarlet Witch — Mono-Red Big Mana
subtitle: Bracket 3 · 3/3 Game Changers · no infinite combos · 100 cards · finalized 2026-08-02
footer: Discount = Wanda's power + Ruby Medallion + Longshot, generic only, MV 4+ only. Crackle: X costs 3 generic each and deals 5X. X=8 is 40 = a kill from full. Free-casting an X-spell forces X=0. Full pilot notes in research/gameplan.md and research/formulas.md.

in.name: Urabrask
in.text: 4/4 first strike. Whenever you cast an instant or sorcery, deals 1 to target opponent AND adds {R}. Flips into a Saga once you've cast three in a turn.

out.name: Molten-Core Maestro
out.text: Opus — whenever you cast an instant/sorcery, put a +1/+1 counter on it. If 5+ mana was spent, add {R} equal to its power.

swaps.why: Measured, not guessed: Maestro's mana ability needs 5+ mana SPENT, and only 6 of 37 fixed-cost instants/sorceries still cost that much after a 2-power discount. Wanda's discount actively turns it off — the better she is, the less it triggers. Urabrask's {R} is unconditional.
swaps.back: Only if the deck somehow stops discounting.

in.name: Ashling, Flame Dancer
in.text: 4/4. Keeps unspent red mana across steps. Loots on every instant/sorcery; 2nd resolution each turn deals 2 to each opponent and their creatures; 3rd adds {R}{R}{R}{R}.

out.name: Fellwar Stone
out.text: {T}: Add one mana of any colour a land an opponent controls could produce.

swaps.why: A build error being corrected. In mono-red, Fellwar Stone often cannot produce {R} at all — and the deck has {R}{R} and {R}{R}{R} costs throughout. Ashling both fixes flood (loot every spell) and produces mana.
swaps.back: Tables where every opponent plays red.

in.name: Hex Magic
in.text: Exile your whole hand, draw that many, and you may still play the exiled cards until the end of your next turn.

out.name: Rousing Refrain
out.text: Add {R} for each card in target opponent's hand, retained until end of turn. Suspend 3—{1}{R}.

swaps.why: Rousing Refrain scales off your OPPONENTS' hand sizes — dead against a table that has dumped its grip. Hex Magic is reliable, cheaper, and effectively doubles your available cards for the turn.
swaps.back: Full-grip tables: control, counterspell decks, Rhystic/Remora pods. Three opponents holding four cards each is 12 red mana.

in.name: Wiccan, Young Avenger
in.text: 3/3. Whenever you cast a noncreature spell, exile the top card of your library — you may play it until your next end step.

out.name: Call Forth the Tempest
out.text: Cascade, cascade. Deals damage to each creature opponents control equal to the total MV of your other spells this turn.

swaps.why: Impulse card advantage on EVERY noncreature spell — a six-spell turn draws six extra cards, for 24 cents. Tempest was eight mana with a random cascade.
swaps.back: Creature-heavy boards where the sweep half matters.

in.name: Neheb, the Eternal
in.text: 4/6 afflict 3. At the beginning of each of your postcombat main phases, add {R} for each 1 life your opponents have lost this turn.

out.name: Comet Storm
out.text: Multikicker {1}. Deals X damage to each of up to 1 + kicks targets.

swaps.why: A Fiery-Confluence turn hands you 18+ red mana in your second main phase. Comet Storm was redundant with Crackle with Power, which does the same job better.
swaps.back: When you want a second instant-speed X-spell.

in.name: Disrupt Decorum
in.text: Goad all creatures you don't control — until your next turn they must attack, and must attack someone other than you.

out.name: Blazing Crescendo
out.text: Target creature gets +3/+1. Exile the top card of your library; you may play it until the end of your next turn.

swaps.why: Reversal of an earlier bad cut. The deck had NO way to avoid being attacked, and red gets no fogs. Goad is a one-sided fog that also points the table at each other. Crescendo was outclassed by Monstrous Rage anyway — same +3/+1 for half the mana, plus a permanent +1/+1 Role.
swaps.back: If you want a sixth pump effect.

in.name: Champion's Helm
in.text: Equipped creature gets +2/+2 and, while it's legendary, has hexproof. Equip {1}.

out.name: Swiftfoot Boots
out.text: Equipped creature has hexproof and haste. Equip {1}.

swaps.why: A swap, not redundancy — hexproof does not stack. Haste is worth nothing here because Wanda's discount is a STATIC ability that works the moment she resolves. The +2/+2 is +2 off every discounted spell, and 10 of our 12 creatures are legendary.
swaps.back: Artifact-removal-heavy pods, or if you want haste for the Blackblade commander-damage line.

in.name: Fiery Confluence
in.text: Choose three, repeats allowed: 1 damage to each creature / 2 damage to each opponent / destroy target artifact.

out.name: Insurrection
out.text: Untap all creatures and gain control of them until end of turn. They gain haste.

swaps.why: MV 4, so Wanda drops it to {R}{R} — six damage to each opponent for two mana, or a three-damage sweeper. Insurrection is six mana after the discount, wins through COMBAT (the one axis this deck isn't built for), and is blank against a creature-light table.
swaps.back: Creature-heavy boards worth stealing. Note it is NOT a defensive card — it's a sorcery and can't answer an attack.

in.name: Volcanic Vision
in.text: Return an instant/sorcery from your graveyard to hand; deals damage equal to that card's MV to each creature YOUR OPPONENTS control. Exiles itself.

out.name: Wild Ricochet
out.text: Change targets of target instant/sorcery, then copy it.

swaps.why: MV 7 → {3}{R}{R}. Return Apex of Power and it's a 10-damage ONE-SIDED wipe plus the regrowth — it doesn't kill your own engines. Wild Ricochet was the fourth redirect behind Deflecting Swat, Bolt Bend and Return the Favor.
swaps.back: Spell-heavy pods where redirect-and-copy earns its slot.

in.name: Fiery Inscription
in.text: Whenever you cast an instant or sorcery, deals 2 damage to each opponent. On entry, the Ring tempts you.

out.name: Double Vision
out.text: Whenever you cast your first instant or sorcery each turn, copy it.

swaps.why: Three mana for 2 to each opponent per spell — a five-spell turn is 30 damage across the table — and being an enchantment it survives the removal that kills Thor and Longshot. Double Vision was five mana to copy a single spell per turn.
swaps.back: Grindy games where you cast one spell a turn for many turns.

in.name: Solphim, Mayhem Dominus
in.text: 5/4. Doubles all noncombat damage you deal to opponents and to permanents they control. Can give itself an indestructible counter.

out.name: Fiery Emancipation
out.text: Triples all damage from sources you control.

swaps.why: Two mana cheaper, and it doubles ONLY damage aimed at opponents — Fiery Emancipation triples damage to your own board too, which would make Blasphemous Act read 39 to each creature. Neither gets Wanda's discount (creature and enchantment), so the two-mana gap is the whole argument. Solphim halves the X you need on Crackle.
swaps.back: If you want the triple instead of the double and can afford six mana.

in.name: Mithril Coat
in.text: Flash. Indestructible. On entry, attach it to target legendary creature you control. Equipped creature has indestructible.

out.name: Blasphemous Act
out.text: Costs {1} less for each creature on the battlefield. Deals 13 damage to each creature.

swaps.why: The deck had no answer to a board wipe: hexproof does nothing (a wrath doesn't target), Commander's Plate's protection doesn't stop a destroy effect and gives nothing vs red, and all three redirects need a spell with a single target. Mithril Coat has FLASH, so you hold it and deploy in response. Blasphemous Act was also the only sweeper that killed Wanda — and the claim it 'pairs with the damage doublers' fails, since 13 already kills everything and it deals no damage to players.
swaps.back: Tables with LARGE creatures, where Chandra's Ignition at low power and Fiery Confluence at 3 don't get there.

upgrades.title: Bracket 4 upgrade path
upgrades.intro: Swap these 14 and the Bracket 3 list becomes the Bracket 4 list in DECK-B4.md — 86 cards stay the same. The fair mana base becomes a fast one and Underworld Breach turns the graveyard into a second hand. Everything costing 5+ that isn't a payoff comes out. Game Changers go from 3 to 10, which is legal at Bracket 4 and NOT at Bracket 3.

in.name: Mana Vault
in.text: {T}: Add {C}{C}{C}. Doesn't untap normally; {4}: Untap. 1 damage per upkeep it stays tapped.

out.name: Mind Stone
out.text: {T}: Add {C}. {1},{T}, Sacrifice: Draw a card.

swaps.why: Bracket 4 wants explosive mana on turns 1–3, not a fair rock that ramps by one. Three mana off a one-drop.
swaps.back: Always — Mana Vault is a Game Changer and B3 caps at three.

in.name: Grim Monolith
in.text: {T}: Add {C}{C}{C}. Doesn't untap during your untap step; {4}: Untap.

out.name: Tablet of Discovery
out.text: ETB mill a card, may play it this turn. {T}: Add {R}. {T}: Add {R}{R}, instants and sorceries only.

swaps.why: Net +1 mana the turn it lands instead of a three-mana rock that produces two.
swaps.back: Always — Game Changer.

in.name: Chrome Mox
in.text: Imprint: exile a nonland, nonartifact card from hand. {T}: Add one mana of the imprinted card's colour.

out.name: Pyromancer's Goggles
out.text: {T}: Add {R}. When that mana is spent on a red instant/sorcery, copy that spell.

swaps.why: Goggles is a five-mana investment that pays off a turn later. B4 needs turn-one acceleration more than a delayed copy engine.
swaps.back: Always — Game Changer. Goggles is one of the best cards in the fair build: the copy keeps X and can re-use targets.

in.name: Mox Diamond
in.text: If this would enter, discard a land card instead or bin it. {T}: Add one mana of any colour.

out.name: Brass's Bounty
out.text: Create a Treasure for each land you control — untapped.

swaps.why: Brass's Bounty is 5 mana after the discount for ~14 untapped Treasures, which is enormous but a turn-7 card. B4 is trying to win by then.
swaps.back: Always — Game Changer. Brass's Bounty is the fair build's biggest single mana burst.

in.name: Mox Amber
in.text: {T}: Add one mana of any colour among legendary creatures and planeswalkers you control.

out.name: Reforge the Soul
out.text: Each player discards their hand, then draws seven. Miracle {1}{R}.

swaps.why: Wanda switches Mox Amber on by herself, and B4 already runs Wheel of Fortune, Will of the Jeskai and Faithless Looting.
swaps.back: The miracle cost makes Reforge a two-mana Wheel whenever you draw it first — watch every draw step.

in.name: Lotus Petal
in.text: {T}, Sacrifice: Add one mana of any colour.

out.name: Monstrous Rage
out.text: Target creature gets +2/+0 and a Monster Role token (+1/+1, trample).

swaps.why: The pump package shrinks to three in B4 — the fast build wins before growing Wanda pays off.
swaps.back: The permanent +1/+1 Role is a permanent discount in the fair build.

in.name: Lion's Eye Diamond
in.text: {T}, Discard your hand, Sacrifice: Add three mana of any one colour.

out.name: Blackblade Reforged
out.text: Equipped creature gets +1/+1 for each land you control. Equip legendary {3}, equip {7}.

swaps.why: LED is the other half of Underworld Breach — discarding your hand is upside once Breach is out. Blackblade is a five-mana all-in that deals no damage the turn it lands.
swaps.back: Always — Game Changer. Blackblade is the biggest single discount boost in the fair build.

in.name: City of Traitors
in.text: {T}: Add {C}{C}. When you play another land, sacrifice this.

out.name: Mountain
out.text: Basic Land — Mountain.

swaps.why: Two mana off one land pulls the Breach turn forward by a full turn cycle.
swaps.back: The fair build wants stable mana more than a burst, and Valakut counts Mountains.

in.name: Underworld Breach
in.text: Each nonland card in your graveyard has escape — its mana cost plus exile three other cards. Sacrifice it at end step.

out.name: Arcane Bombardment
out.text: First instant/sorcery each turn: exile one at random from your yard, then copy every card exiled with it, free.

swaps.why: Breach turns the graveyard into a second hand, and because escape cost equals the mana cost, X-SPELLS ESCAPE AT FULL SIZE. Arcane Bombardment's copies are free-cast, so they force X=0.
swaps.back: Always — Game Changer, and it enables lines a fair pod won't enjoy.

in.name: Gamble
in.text: Search your library for a card, put it into your hand, then discard a card at random.

out.name: Improvisation Capstone
out.text: Exile from the top until total MV 4+, cast any number free. Paradigm: a free copy from exile at the start of each of your first main phases.

swaps.why: A one-mana tutor for Breach or Crackle. The random discard barely matters once Breach can escape whatever you lose.
swaps.back: Always — Game Changer. Capstone's Paradigm is a recurring engine the fair build wants.

in.name: Reiterate
in.text: Buyback {3}. Copy target instant or sorcery spell.

out.name: Zuko's Exile
out.text: Exile target artifact, creature or enchantment. Its controller creates a Clue.

swaps.why: Reiterate with buyback plus Mana Geyser is infinite mana, and it copies X-spells at full size.
swaps.back: ALWAYS. This is the single card that would make the Bracket 3 list an infinite combo deck — it must never appear there.

in.name: Finale of Promise
in.text: Cast up to one instant and one sorcery from your graveyard with MV X or less, free. If X is 10+, copy each twice.

out.name: Disrupt Decorum
out.text: Goad all creatures you don't control.

swaps.why: B4 wins before the crack-back matters, so the fog is worth less than a second recursion spell.
swaps.back: Disrupt Decorum is the fair build's ONLY way to not be attacked.

in.name: Dance with Calamity
in.text: Exile cards from the top one at a time; while the total MV stays 13 or less you may cast any number of them free.

out.name: Fiery Inscription
out.text: Whenever you cast an instant or sorcery, deals 2 damage to each opponent.

swaps.why: A chip clock needs several turns and B4 doesn't have several turns. Dance converts a big mana pile straight into a board.
swaps.back: Fiery Inscription is 30+ damage over a normal fair-length game.

in.name: Faithless Looting
in.text: Draw two cards, then discard two. Flashback {2}{R}.

out.name: Solphim, Mayhem Dominus
out.text: Doubles noncombat damage you deal to opponents and their permanents.

swaps.why: Looting fills the graveyard for Underworld Breach, so discarding is upside. Solphim does nothing on an empty board.
swaps.back: Solphim halves the X you need on Crackle, which is the fair build's entire kill.

sideboard.name: Blasphemous Act
sideboard.when: IN for Volcanic Vision, vs boards with LARGE creatures where Chandra's Ignition at low power and Fiery Confluence at 3 don't get there. Costs {1} less per creature on the battlefield — often {R}. Remember it kills Wanda too.

sideboard.name: Rousing Refrain
sideboard.when: IN for Mana Geyser, vs full-grip tables — control, counterspell decks, Rhystic Study / Mystic Remora pods. Three opponents holding four cards each is 12 red mana. Dead against aggro.

sideboard.name: Insurrection
sideboard.when: IN for Chandra's Ignition, vs creature-heavy boards worth stealing. NOT a defensive card — it's a sorcery, so it cannot answer an attack.

sideboard.name: Swiftfoot Boots
sideboard.when: IN for Champion's Helm, vs artifact-removal-heavy pods, or when you want haste for the Blackblade commander-damage line. Hexproof does not stack.

sideboard.name: Darksteel Plate
sideboard.when: IN for Return the Favor, when you want a SECOND indestructible source. Five mana all-in and no flash, so it's strictly worse than Mithril Coat.

sideboard.name: Nova Flame
sideboard.when: IN for Volcanic Vision, vs creature decks. The +1/+1 counters on Wanda are PERMANENT, so the discount grows — but it deals no damage to players and can't close.

sideboard.name: Prisoner's Dilemma
sideboard.when: IN for Fiery Confluence, vs pods that enjoy politics. 4/8/12 damage to each opponent, but THEY choose the outcome.

sideboard.name: Pinnacle Monk
sideboard.when: IN for a Mountain, if you keep flooding or getting land-screwed. The spell half is a CREATURE, so Wanda never discounts it, and Mystic Peak isn't a Mountain — it turns off Valakut and adds no Nykthos devotion.

sideboard.name: Hit the Mother Lode
sideboard.when: IN for Tablet of Discovery. Discover 10 free-casts your best card. Its Treasures enter TAPPED, so that mana is for next turn — and Brass's Bounty makes ~14 untapped for the same 5 mana.

sideboard.name: Jaya's Immolating Inferno
sideboard.when: IN for Electrodominance, when you want a second Crackle. X damage to up to three targets, all different. The legendary requirement is always met.

sideboard.name: Fiery Emancipation
sideboard.when: IN for Solphim, if you want the triple instead of the double. Six mana, an enchantment so NO discount, and it triples damage to your own board too.

sideboard.name: Comet Storm
sideboard.when: IN for Electrodominance, when you want a second instant-speed X-spell. Multikicker {1} per extra target.

sideboard.name: Call Forth the Tempest
sideboard.when: IN for Apex of Power, vs creature-heavy boards. Cascade twice, then damage to each creature opponents control equal to the total MV of your other spells this turn.

sideboard.name: Wild Ricochet
sideboard.when: IN for Untimely Malfunction, vs spell-heavy pods. Redirect AND copy. It was the fourth redirect behind Deflecting Swat, Bolt Bend and Return the Favor.

sideboard.name: Double Vision
sideboard.when: IN for Repeated Reverberation, in grindy games where you cast one spell a turn for many turns. Copies only your FIRST instant/sorcery each turn.

sideboard.name: Blazing Crescendo
sideboard.when: IN for Monstrous Rage, if you want a sixth pump. Outclassed — Monstrous Rage is the same +3/+1 for half the mana and leaves a permanent +1/+1 Role.

sideboard.name: Witch's Mark
sideboard.when: IN for Monstrous Rage, in grindy tables where the extra card beats tempo. MV 2 so no discount, but the Wicked Role is a permanent +1 to Wanda's power.

sideboard.name: Coruscation Mage
sideboard.when: IN for Fiery Inscription, vs low-interaction tables where a chip clock survives. Offspring {2} gives a second body. Dies to any wipe.

sideboard.name: Molten-Core Maestro
sideboard.when: IN for Storm-Kiln Artist, only if the deck somehow stops discounting. Its mana ability needs 5+ mana SPENT, and only 6 of 37 fixed-cost spells cost that after a 2-power discount — Wanda actively turns it off.

sideboard.name: Fellwar Stone
sideboard.when: IN for Mind Stone, only at tables with red opponents. In mono-red it often cannot produce {R} at all, and the deck has {R}{R} and {R}{R}{R} costs throughout.
